races.name: Norfolk Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: Won on debut over this trip on good ground but was beaten sixth at Royal Ascot on latest start; a natural prominent racer who is unlikely to find the front-row berth he needs in a 21-runner field, and that positional compromise slightly blunts his chance.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up in a novice at Wolverhampton last time by three lengths, but that form needs boosting further as this is a significant step up in class; bred for speed and effective at today's trip, but ranked 18th of 21 on our figures, making this a tough ask from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Blake's Monarch
runners_data.note: Placed at 6f on good ground and showed speed, but a drop to 5f with a busy field of fast rivals questions whether he can secure his favoured prominent pitch; trainer Furtado has modest 14-day form and the weight of numbers works against him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Blake's Monarch looks out of its depth stepping up in class here, despite showing fair form on turf debut at Chester 21 days ago and proven effectiveness at the trip on good ground.

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partner for Aidan O'Brien with a 1-2-1 recent record including a 5f win on good ground; a natural front-rank runner who is one of the more likely to actually press forward despite the crowded pace scenario, and Moore's positional instincts are a genuine asset.
runners_data.comment: Carry The Flag arrives here on the back of a fine Group 3 second at The Curragh, beaten just a length and a quarter while stepping up in class and showing sharp early pace; a big, strong type with a top jockey aboard, the five furlongs here may actually bring out the best in this high-class prospect.

runners_data.name: El Floridita
runners_data.note: Won over 5f good ground and has the pace to race prominently, but finished fifth when stepped up to stronger company; Nigel Tinkler sends her here on the back of that experience, and she will look to go forward even if the map has her mid-pack.
runners_data.comment: Showed improved form when taking a maiden at Redcar last time, but that win came with caveats and this represents a sharp step up in grade for a recent purchase. Drawn 8, handles today's trip and conditions, yet ranks 16th of 21 on our figures — hard to get excited.

runners_data.name: Flight Signal
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in one start, winning over 5f on good ground under James Doyle for Archie Watson — a sharp profile — but the single run leaves her form lightly tested; she is a genuine early mover who will try to get to the front and is one of the key pace threats behind Where Love Lives.
runners_data.comment: Burst clear by three-and-a-quarter lengths on debut at Bath, Flight Signal looks a promising type who acts on this going and trip, though stepping up sharply in class from a novice on just one start is the obvious query at a mark of 129lb from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Force Noir
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good ground and placed on Tapeta; headgear (blinkers) suggests he needs to be switched on, and his truly prominent nature is pushed rearward by the field volume — a fast pace would arguably suit him more than a controlled one, and the blinkers may help him focus.
runners_data.comment: Blinkers fitted for the first time as Force Noir returns after a 54-day break, and that Naas maiden win — striding clear by 4¼ lengths on better ground — showed a willing attitude with more to come; the trip and track look suitable, though stall 19 and 129 lb are worth noting.

runners_data.name: Mr Macartney
runners_data.note: Chequered form string of 4-1-7-6 suggests inconsistency; won over 5f on good ground but has also struggled in larger fields — the visor is fitted, and his natural forwardness is squeezed out by sheer numbers in this race; Oli Rix has no runners in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Beaten two lengths in a Listed contest at Sandown 23 days ago, Mr Macartney has course-and-distance form to his name and steps up in trip wearing a visor for the first time, which could unlock improvement — though his recent sixth and seventh suggest he's yet to recapture that winning thread.

runners_data.name: Mussab
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partner for Richard and Peter Fahey, with only a third-place debut over 6f on good ground to his name; lightly raced and style unknown, so there is significant opacity around how he will be ridden and whether the drop to 5f suits.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise on debut, finishing third beaten just 1¼ lengths at York in novice company, and Mussab clearly handles today's trip and good ground well enough — but the step up in class is a concern, and greenness under pressure could be costly again from stall 14.

runners_data.name: New Yorker
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien hold-up horse with a progressive record — won over 5f soft ground then placed twice on good — but Wayne Lordan will need a fast pace to soften up the leaders; five furlongs on good-to-firm Ascot with a moderate pace is not his ideal canvas.
runners_data.comment: Hooded for the first time and steadily building through recent starts, but ranked 15th of 21 on our figures and the speed rating of 33 makes this a tough ask; sprint-bred and effective over today's trip on good ground, though this looks a step too far at present.

runners_data.name: Orthodox
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 5f on good ground for Clive Cox under Rossa Ryan; fits the prominent-chaser mould perfectly and is exactly the profile the pace map favours — one clear run tracking the leader in a race where only one horse has the pace to lead.
runners_data.comment: Impressive on debut, winning a Salisbury maiden by 2½ lengths on good ground over today's trip, but that's just one run to go on; bred for speed and thought highly of, though stall 16 and a 37-day absence from a lightly raced sort introduce some uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Persian Spring
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground and was pulled up when stepped up in trip; the drop back to 5f under Jamie Spencer is interesting — Spencer is an astute reader of pace and will place him in a perfect tracking position if the single front-runner scenario unfolds cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Successful over today's trip and going when landing a York novice last time out, Persian Spring enters from stall 10 carrying 129 lb, though the step back in distance raises a question — better may yet come, but the trip could blunt that progress.

runners_data.name: Savage Mariner
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's second-run horse placed over 6f on good ground; lightly raced and style undetermined, pushed rearward on the map due to field composition; five furlongs first time at the track requires him to adapt quickly.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise on debut, going down by just 1½ lengths at Leicester, and the step back to 6f looks a natural fit — though the drop in trip isn't guaranteed to unlock improvement. Carries 129 lb from stall 20 yet to score, but there's potential here.

runners_data.name: Social Symbol
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good ground under William Buick for the Crisfords just 17 days ago — a sharp, quick turnaround that speaks of trainer confidence; Buick will position him immediately behind Where Love Lives and is one of the best-placed horses for the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Sole start produced a half-length debut win at Ripon 17 days ago — form since franked and scope for improvement stepping up in class, but ranked 19th of 21 on our figures here, making this a significant jump from novice company at stall 18 carrying 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Glory
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on firm ground and placed over 6f; Charles Hills sends her here on the back of a 39-day break; Jason Watson rides and she has the profile to creep into contention from a prominent berth if the pace settles.
runners_data.comment: Beaten on debut before getting off the mark in a Bath novice last time — overcoming a slow start and trouble in running to score by 2½l — Sovereign Glory arrives 39 days later with a case for progressing further, and the 5-6f trip on fast ground suits; but ranked 20 of 21 on our figures, stall 17 and 129lb make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Star Prospect
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's runner placed over 5f good and won over 5f soft; Dylan Browne McMonagle is one of the most in-form young riders in Europe and will aim to sit in the chasing group, though the step up in class from his soft-ground maiden win is a question.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win before finishing a staying-on third at Naas last time, Star Prospect looks to have more improvement in the locker and takes well to this trip and varied ground; the 129 lb burden from stall 7 is the one query.

runners_data.name: Tribeca
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground for Robson De Aguiar; the slight concern is whether he truly has the raw speed for five furlongs in a Group 2 as opposed to a longer trip, and the 56-day gap since his last run is the longest fresher in the field.
runners_data.comment: Tribeca took his debut maiden at Navan in authoritative fashion, always holding sway throughout, but returns here after 56 days off and faces a step up in class; effective at today's trip and suited by sounder ground, this promising colt has the tools but remains unexposed.

runners_data.name: Underdog
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good ground for Richard Spencer only eight days ago — by far the quickest turnaround in the field — and Saffie Osborne keeps the ride; the rapid return from a straightforward win can be a positive sign of trainer confidence, but recovery time is minimal.
runners_data.comment: Debut winner at Sandown, beating more experienced rivals with a sharp turn of foot, but stepping up considerably in class here and our figures rank it 17th of 21; the in-form trainer and speedy pedigree offer slim encouragement, yet this looks a tough ask on ratings.

runners_data.name: Where Love Lives
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's two-time winner over 5f on good ground under Kevin Stott, and the only confirmed front-runner in the race; she is the key pace-setter and her ability to dictate terms without pressure makes her central to how every scenario unfolds.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in its last two starts, Where Love Lives is a big, powerful type still maturing and looks to have more improvement in the locker after taking Listed honours at Sandown last time; the slight hesitation before finding top gear is the one concern to keep in mind.

runners_data.name: Ez Tina
runners_data.note: Wesley Ward's American-trained filly, blinkers fitted, going experience unknown on turf; Ward's runners habitually burst from the gates and thrive in fast-paced sprints, which is a genuine fit for the good-to-firm surface if she handles the track.
runners_data.comment: Showed plenty of pace when winning by five lengths on debut at Woodbine, and the step into this 21-runner field from stall 3 is a neutral factor; first-time blinkers could sharpen the focus, though whether she sees out the trip under 126 lb remains the key question.

runners_data.name: Fanshell Beach
runners_data.note: Second Ward runner with blinkers, won on her only start and handled by James McDonald who has strong experience riding in Europe; the going is an unknown variable, but Ward's stable pattern over 5f at Royal Ascot is well established and she should be respected.
runners_data.comment: Impressive on debut at Churchill Downs — winning by 5¼ lengths despite a slow start — Fanshell Beach arrives from stall 11 carrying 126 lb with first-time blinkers as the stable's second string, and while our rating of 115 underlines the form, stamina for this longer trip remains the key question.

runners_data.name: Through The Years
runners_data.note: Ward's third runner, placed over a sprint trip and handled by veteran John Velazquez; style is unclear from UK data but Ward's horses habitually press the pace, and Velazquez's gate-to-wire instincts on turf may translate well to a 5f straight sprint.
runners_data.comment: Backed up a debut run with a convincing Fillies & Mares victory at Belmont last time, and acts well on firm ground, but stable form has taken a few knocks this week and first-time blinkers add an element of the unknown for this stall-15 runner.

races.paceDynamic: Where Love Lives is the one confirmed front-runner and, with only one natural pace-setter in a 21-runner field, she is likely to be allowed to stride into a clear lead from the outset and set a tempo she controls rather than one forced upon her. The going is Good to Firm throughout Ascot, which rewards early speed and efficient movement rather than grinding it out late, so a front-runner dictating a sustainable gallop on this surface is in a powerful tactical position. Horses who can sit just off the pace in the slipstream — Social Symbol, Orthodox, Persian Spring, Carry The Flag, Flight Signal, and the Ward trio — are the profiles best placed to challenge, as a smooth pace transition at the two-furlong pole will suit those tracking rather than those making up ground from the rear. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can physically hold their natural position; of those redistributed into midfield, Flight Signal, Carry The Flag and El Floridita are the most likely to actually press forward and contest a place near the pace. The race shape firmly favours prominent racers tracking the leader in a disciplined position, because the uncontested pace will be fair rather than fierce, giving no real acceleration incentive to pure hold-up horses who will find themselves with too much ground to make up in only five furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Where Love Lives is uncontested at the front — watch whether Kevin Stott presses early to build a lead or settles into a controlled rhythm, as that decision will define whether the front-runner holds on or the chasers reel her in.

The three Wesley Ward American runners (Ez Tina, Fanshell Beach, Through The Years) all wear blinkers and typically blast from the gates — if any of them press Where Love Lives hard from the outset, the pace dynamic shifts from controlled to contested and the entire field faces a different race shape.

Flight Signal and Carry The Flag are both natural front-runners squeezed into a midfield map position — watch the early stages for these two trying to push forward, as their presence near the pace could either disrupt the front or establish a two-horse lead scenario that benefits neither.

With 21 runners on a straight 5f, wide draws and early traffic are a genuine concern — horses drawn wide who miss the break or get caught in traffic for even one furlong face near-impossible tasks at this trip on good-to-firm ground.

Force Noir (blinkers) and Mr Macartney (visor) are both headgear-equipped prominent types pushed to the rear — if either makes an unexpected forward move from their drawn position, they could become pace disruptors rather than pace victims.

races.name: Hardwicke Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Amiloc
runners_data.note: Ran well in similar good ground conditions and has form over the trip, but as a natural front-runner who will find himself racing in a constrained midfield role due to the traffic of prominent types ahead, his chance is tempered by being unable to produce his best from an unnatural position.
runners_data.comment: Won the King Edward VII Stakes here last year, but pulled hard and faded when too fresh at York last time (36 days ago); with that run now in the tank a revival is plausible, though ranked 9 of 12 on our figures this looks a notably stronger test.

runners_data.name: Best Secret
runners_data.note: Won impressively at Deauville last time out and has a sharp recent French form line, but limited Ascot experience and only two runs on similar going; as a horse who naturally races prominently, being pushed into a midfield slot reduces his chance of landing a telling blow.
runners_data.comment: Thriving form — three wins in its last five starts, the most recent a convincing Group 3 success at Longchamp — but Best Secret returns after 48 days and steps up markedly in class; the galloping track suits a big, progressive type, though the 129 lb burden is a genuine test.

runners_data.name: Ethical Diamond
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' six-year-old was dominant in his three straight wins on fast ground and showed Ascot form with a big run in the Coronation Cup last time; races genuinely prominently and has the class to sit just behind Jan Brueghel if given the chance, making him a key player in the forward group.
runners_data.comment: Wearing a hood for the first time and back after 84 days, Ethical Diamond's Dubai reappearance — beaten 6½ lengths — is best set aside given that progressive C&D-winning profile, yet our figures rank this 11th of 12 and a career-best effort may be required.

runners_data.name: Giavellotto
runners_data.note: Consistent sort for Marco Botti with strong good-ground form — three of his last five on similar conditions — and Oisin Murphy's booking adds confidence; lacks a recent win but his place record is rock solid, and he should travel comfortably in a prominent midfield position.
runners_data.comment: Consistent, well-travelled performer and former Hong Kong Vase winner, Giavellotto was 4¼ lengths back in third last time at Group 1 level, running his race without troubling the best — 84 days off could blunt his edge, though a top jockey returns and he handles today's conditions.

runners_data.name: Goliath
runners_data.note: Won the Prix Ganay last time and ran a solid second in the Coronation Cup the run before, both on good ground; Soumillon rides positively and the five-year-old's profile — consistent, good-ground performer over this trip — fits the likely race shape extremely well.
runners_data.comment: Twice a G1 winner and a former C&D scorer now back to his best, Goliath arrives on the back of a comfortable Group 2 success 20 days ago — form figures reading 1-2-3 in his last three — and handles today's distance and going well; the worry is that one rival has matched him closely in recent encounters.

runners_data.name: Jan Brueghel
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter in the race; Ryan Moore will control proceedings from the front at a tempo of his choosing, and with four wins in nine career starts and strong good-going form, his chance is significant — though he has previously found one or two too good when the race quickens late.
runners_data.comment: Dual-distance winner and St Leger champion in 2024, Jan Brueghel arrives on a 14-day turnaround with a proven jockey aboard and connections who have a strong record in this race — though the testing ground that cost him dearly at Epsom last time remains the key concern.

runners_data.name: Lambourn
runners_data.note: Has five wins from eleven and two O'Brien stablemates in the race complicate the tactical picture; mapped to a hold-up position despite being a naturally prominent type — the least pace-committed of the prominent group pushed back — which is far from ideal given his preference for racing forward.
runners_data.comment: Placed at the top level and a proven Group 1 winner over course and distance, Lambourn arrives 14 days after being sent into an overly prominent position in the Coronation Cup, paying for it with a 16-length defeat; first-time cheekpieces and a tempered approach may help, but the 129 lb burden and signs of awkwardness suggest this is likely the stable's supporting act.

runners_data.name: Phantom Flight
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back races earlier this season and has strong course and distance form, but his last run was a well-beaten sixth at this level; as a horse who wants to race prominently but will be swallowed into midfield here, his ability to produce a winning effort from that position is genuinely in doubt.
runners_data.comment: Beaten comfortably in a Group 3 on its latest start, Phantom Flight may still need time to re-acclimatise after a Middle East campaign and, ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, is hard to fancy despite a trainer in form and proven stamina at this trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sons And Lovers
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's five-year-old has winning form over extended trips in good ground but has not threatened at the top level recently; a natural front-runner who will be unable to secure his preferred slot and is therefore carrying a meaningful style-fit penalty in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces go on for the first time here, and Sons And Lovers does boast a couple of wins in its last five starts — but two consecutive fourths, including an eight-length beating in a Group 3 latest, suggest this step into deeper waters is a tough ask, ranking last on our figures.

runners_data.name: West Wind Blows
runners_data.note: Simon and Ed Crisford's seven-year-old has a remarkable recent record — five consecutive runner-up finishes — suggesting high consistency but also a tendency to find one too good; similarly to Lambourn, he has been pushed back from his natural prominent position due to field size, which is unlikely to suit.
runners_data.comment: Desperately consistent at the top level, West Wind Blows went agonisingly close in a Group 3 at Newbury last time, going down by a neck, and acts on any ground over this trip; the concern is that a couple of today's rivals have finished ahead of him lately.

runners_data.name: Kalpana
runners_data.note: Won consecutive Listed and Group races on good ground over 1m2f-1m4f, and Andrew Balding's five-year-old mare arrives in excellent form with Colin Keane, who rides prominently when conditions allow; her penalty weight difference (126lbs versus the rest at 129lbs) is a genuine small advantage at this level on quick ground.
runners_data.comment: Kalpana arrives here in back-to-back winning form, including a G1 success over course and distance, and a narrow Group 3 victory last time that came despite racing a touch keenly and feeling the run close home — both concerns now resolved; first-time cheekpieces on a top-class filly who may still have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Santorini Star
runners_data.note: William Haggas's five-year-old has a good form line including two wins and a placed effort in good ground over the trip; carries headgear and is a natural prominent racer who will be displaced into midfield given the pace traffic — his style-fit concern is the main reservation against him despite smart recent form.
runners_data.comment: Santorini Star arrives in cheekpieces for the first time off a solid run — beaten a short-neck at Group 1 level last time — and clearly has upward momentum over 12-16f on any surface, but this sharper trip may just stretch its speed reserves against stronger company.

races.paceDynamic: Jan Brueghel is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with Ryan Moore aboard, is likely to control this from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f at Ascot — a track that rewards horses who can dominate from the front and quicken when asked. The majority of the field — Amiloc, Best Secret, Phantom Flight, Sons And Lovers, Santorini Star and others — are all naturally prominent types who cannot all get their preferred position, meaning several will have to race in a more restrained midfield role against their instincts, which may cause early friction and unsettle their rhythms. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure a position near the pace; Jan Brueghel is most likely to lead, with Ethical Diamond, Goliath and Kalpana the most likely to actually get close to the pace given their class and jockey quality. The race shape strongly favours horses who can either track Jan Brueghel from a genuine prominent position or those with the class and acceleration to travel smoothly in midfield and pick up when the race quickens in the straight — a steadily-run race at a sustainable pace on quick ground is most likely to suit prominent trackers and strong-finishing mid-division horses with a high cruising speed.

watchPoints.text: Jan Brueghel — if Ryan Moore rolls along unchallenged from the front, monitor whether any other prominent types (Goliath, Ethical Diamond) can get close enough to challenge turning in; if they cannot, Jan Brueghel could simply quicken clear.

Prominent group crowding — with Amiloc, Best Secret, Phantom Flight, Sons And Lovers and Santorini Star all naturally wanting to race forward but forced into midfield, watch for bumping, shuffling or riders losing rhythm in the first half-mile.

Kalpana's weight advantage — at 126lbs versus the field's 129lbs, a small but meaningful edge on fast ground over 1m4f; if she gets a clean, prominent trip behind Jan Brueghel, that difference could matter in a close finish.

West Wind Blows and Lambourn — both are naturally prominent types pushed to the rear of the field in this map; if the pace collapses or a late sprint develops, their finishing effort may look more competitive than their mapped position suggests, so do not be surprised if they appear to emerge from "out of nowhere".

Goliath's recent run — just 20 days since his last race, one of the quickest turnarounds in the field; Soumillon manages freshness well but watch for any signs of sourness or edginess in the parade ring that might indicate he is not at his peak so soon after running.

races.name: Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Almeraq
runners_data.note: Useful form on soft and good ground at 6f for Haggas and Marquand, winning last time out; a genuine prominent racer by nature but with relatively few hold-up runners in the field the map places him at the rear — his best chance arrives if he is allowed to take a forward pitch he actually prefers, though the style tag softens the edge of his chance in a rear-drawn shape.|
runners_data.comment: Took the Cathedral Stakes (Listed) at Salisbury by a neck on most recent start 28 days ago, confirming current form, and handles this trip and going well — though fast conditions remain an unknown and there's still a gap to bridge at this level from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Aramram
runners_data.note: Five-year-old sprinter with a solid record at 6f on good/soft for Hannon, placed in this grade before, but his natural front-pressing style is compromised here — with too many prominent types chasing limited forward real estate, Levey may struggle to get him the position he needs to do his best work.|
runners_data.comment: Proven at course and distance and has performed creditably at Group level — including a solid third-placed effort in a Group 2 last time — but ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, and stepping into this grade makes this a considerably stiffer challenge than anything faced before.

runners_data.name: Comanche Brave
runners_data.note: O'Brien-trained four-year-old who won this trip on good last time and has been placed repeatedly in Group company; a committed prominent racer at heart, though the crowded front rank means Boudot is likely forced to settle him slightly further back than ideal — his winning form is almost entirely from the front or second position, which is the key caveat.|
runners_data.comment: Landed the Greenlands Stakes (Group 2) at The Curragh on latest start, quickening clear by two lengths, and has run well at this course before — but ranked 15th of 19 on our figures, making a step up to Group 1 level a tall order at 131lb.

runners_data.name: Great Wish
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Bent Olsen who has won at 6f on Good ground and represents an interesting international angle with Shoemark aboard; front-running by inclination but unable to get that position in this field, with 84 days off the track adding a further layer of uncertainty about peak fitness.|
runners_data.comment: Stepped up to Group 1 company last time, Great Wish was beaten just over two lengths at Meydan — respectable enough, but ranked 17th of 19 on our figures, this looks a tough ask again; the 84-day break and proven effectiveness over 6f on good ground are the main positives.

runners_data.name: Jasour
runners_data.note: True hold-up type for Clive Cox, racing in a tongue-tie, who has struggled repeatedly to land a blow in fields like this — the six consecutive placed/beaten efforts on good ground are a concern but if the pace truly hotts up this is the profile that benefits from a strong end-to-end gallop.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and on a two-year losing run, Jasour faces a stiff task from stall 17 carrying 131 lb, and he often races keenly when his ideal conditions — 6f on fast ground — aren't fully met. First-time headgear is at least worth watching.

runners_data.name: Khaadem
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran for Charles Hills, genuine hold-up specialist under Soumillon, who has won at 6f on firm but recent form in similar conditions has been modest — at his best in truly strongly-run sprints where his staying-power finishes off rivals, which is precisely the scenario this race shape makes hardest.|
runners_data.comment: Landed this prize in both 2023 and 2024, but disappointed on easy ground at Haydock last time out and needs a firm surface to show his best — conditions today are therefore key, and 131lb is a stiff burden if he's still finding his feet.

runners_data.name: Kind Of Blue
runners_data.note: Fanshawe's five-year-old under Buick has shown consistent placed efforts at 6f on Good ground and races prominently enough to get a clean run tracking the pace — placed last time out and showing the kind of repeatable form that suits a race where one horse leads and the chasers fight it out.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent sort who has shown good form on the comeback trail, finishing second on latest outing at York in a Group 2, beaten a length; yet to win in recent starts, and the 131 lb burden is a stern ask, though acts on any ground and is proven at today's trip.

runners_data.name: Lake Forest
runners_data.note: Haggas's OR-119 runner steps back to 6f from recent 7f-8f assignments and that is the primary question mark; Fallon rides and the horse has won at 7f Good but the sprint trip may just stretch his finishing effort at the business end — prominent profile is ideal for the race shape if the trip suits.|
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to form with a dominant Listed success at Haydock last time, beating rivals by five and a half lengths, and handles today's trip and fast surface well; the main risk is whether a 42-day break takes the edge off that sharp comeback.

runners_data.name: Lugal
runners_data.note: Japanese-trained six-year-old under Sameshima who has been placed repeatedly at 6f on Good ground and won over 7f; races prominently and the Ascot straight is not unfamiliar territory in terms of profile, though with 84 days between runs the sharpness needed at this level is a legitimate question.|
runners_data.comment: Placed in a Group 1 Al Quoz Sprint last time out, beaten a neck, and effective at this trip on a sound surface — the form profile has genuine merit — but our figures rank Lugal well down the field, and a Japanese Grade 1 winner in strong form makes further progress essential.

runners_data.name: Overpass
runners_data.note: Australian seven-year-old for Baker who was out just four days ago — that rapid turnaround is the headline angle, and fitness is clearly not a concern; placed three times at this course-and-distance profile and races prominently, though Joshua Parr needs to get him into a comfortable position in a congested front group.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who did plenty of the donkey work when a creditable third in a Group 1 here just four days ago, and that quick turnaround is an obvious concern; a proven G1 performer over this trip and going, though this stiff straight may not play to his prominent style.

runners_data.name: Powerful Glory
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's four-year-old under Spencer has genuine winning form at 6f on Good ground and was last seen finishing seventh in a strong race — the trainer has been in form and the return to Good to Firm conditions is a positive, with Spencer's waiting tactics suiting the prominent-to-midfield slot he may find.|
runners_data.comment: Group 1 winner over course and distance in the autumn, Powerful Glory arrives here 28 days on from a reappearance defeat that should have put an edge on fitness — the main risk is that seventh last time out proves harder to excuse than it looks.

runners_data.name: Regional
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran for Bethell under Rodriguez who has been placed five times at this course and distance configuration — enormously consistent but very difficult to win with at Group 1 level; a natural prominent racer whose map position has shifted to midfield due to field congestion, which is the single biggest factor against him.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts, Regional at least showed consistency when finishing a close third in a Group 2 at York on its comeback 38 days ago, suggesting fitness isn't an issue. First-time headgear and stall 2 are noted, but stepping up in class looks the main obstacle here.

runners_data.name: Sajir
runners_data.note: Fabre's five-year-old under Murphy with three wins at 5f-6f on Good ground and a clear liking for fast conditions — last seen winning at 6f Good and the 20-day turnaround from a French campaign is sharp rather than rushed; races close to the pace and Murphy's ability to position him on the heels of Satono Reve is the key tactical advantage.|
runners_data.comment: Sajir brings a live profile into this: a Group 3 winner last time at Chantilly and a Group 1 scorer over this trip last term, with a trainer in good heart and 20 days' rest suggesting peak fitness. The step back up in distance suits, though the 131 lb burden is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Satono Reve
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner under Moore for Noriyuki Hori, OR-119, with the race shape entirely in his hands — he has won at 6f Good and been placed on the same surface, but the STYLE_FIT tag acknowledges the very fact that his position as lone pace-maker is a role he may not be accustomed to playing against this class; the question is whether Moore over-restrains him or lets him stride.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten just over four lengths when second in a Group 1 at Sha Tin last time, this multiple G1 winner from Japan was arguably unlucky in this same race twelve months ago. First-time headgear adds intrigue, though 55 days off the track is the one query.

runners_data.name: Stolen Kiss
runners_data.note: French-trained four-year-old for Cottier under Pouchin who has won three of his last four in softer conditions (soft/standard), equipped with a tongue-tie; natural prominent racer who arrives on the back of a hat-trick but the switch to Good to Firm ground at the highest level is an unproven commodity — the going is the central doubt.|
runners_data.comment: Progressive dual Listed winner whose three recent victories show sharp current form, but at 131lb from stall 15 wearing a first-time tongue-tie on ground that may not suit, this 47-day absence makes it hard to confidently oppose our bottom-ranked figure here.

runners_data.name: Flora Of Bermuda
runners_data.note: Balding's mare under Doyle won last time at 6f Good and has a strong placed record in Group company on the same surface; a front-running type by character who is likely to find herself slightly further back than she prefers in this field — the key is whether Doyle can get her close enough to the pace to make the most of a proven finishing kick.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent strong traveller who landed a Listed prize at Newmarket on her latest start, though that came 49 days ago and ninth-place effort beforehand clouds the picture slightly; handles today's trip and conditions well, and connections have a strong record at this track.

runners_data.name: Joliestar
runners_data.note: Chris Waller's five-year-old filly under McDonald arrives on the back of three consecutive wins at 6f on good and soft — the hat-trick is compelling, the form is franked, and 77 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh and cherry-ripe; races close to the pace and the Good to Firm conditions are the single question mark against a genuinely strong profile.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins on the bounce, including a hard-fought Group 1 victory at Randwick last time, underline Joliestar's outstanding recent form, and a weight advantage over the chief dangers adds further appeal for a yard with a strong record at this track.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Dariyan
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's four-year-old filly under Loughnane with a win at 6f on Good ground but some patchy recent form including a sixteenth last time in heavy company — the prominent style is natural but will be squeezed in this field, and her OR of 107 at the bottom of the weights is a significant class concern against these rivals.|
runners_data.comment: Third on return to Listed level at Newmarket 49 days ago, Sayidah Dariyan clearly thrives at this course and distance on fast ground, and that run should leave her sharper — though stepping back up to this grade makes life considerably harder from stall 19.

runners_data.name: Time For Sandals
runners_data.note: Eustace's four-year-old filly under Kingscote, last run just four days ago and has been well beaten in recent sprints; a natural prominent-type racer who finds herself mapped to midfield by necessity in this deep field, and recent form figures of 37-580 do not inspire confidence at this level regardless of tactical positioning.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score since taking the Commonwealth Cup over this course and distance last year, Time For Sandals has largely toiled since, most recently beaten six lengths in a Group 1 here after being pushed along too prominently — a quick four-day turnaround makes things no easier from stall 16.

races.paceDynamic: Satono Reve is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — Ryan Moore can slot him out and control the fractions at a sustainable Good to Firm gallop over Ascot's straight six, dictating throughout without being pressured into a suicidal tempo. The pace is real but manageable, meaning Satono Reve can conserve enough to kick again in the final furlong rather than being run off his feet early. With the going reported as Good to Firm (the race card confirms the 3:40 as Good to Firm throughout the day), conditions are fast enough to reward horses who travel smoothly in the first half and finish powerfully, which points clearly toward race-fit prominent-to-handy types who can latch onto the leader's slipstream without burning energy fighting for position. This field is saturated with prominent racers — Comanche Brave, Regional, Flora Of Bermuda, Aramram, Stolen Kiss, Sayidah Dariyan and Time For Sandals all race prominently by nature but cannot all occupy the front rank, meaning the most pace-committed of them will be shuffled back and forced to race out of their comfort zones; Comanche Brave and Kind Of Blue, on ratings and form, are likeliest to actually secure the prominent pitch they need, while the rest face a compromised trip. The race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or just off the pace in second to fourth position and finish with a sustained kick — an uncontested lead with a single pace-setter sets up a shape that punishes genuine hold-up horses and rewards those who can track the tempo, quicken smoothly off Good to Firm ground and hit the line hard.

races.name: Jersey Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Dorset
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien runner with Listed-level form over 7f, has won on soft but form on good is patchier (8th at Royal Ascot last year); a natural prominent type who cannot get that berth in this traffic and will need things to fall kindly from a wider midfield position.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just 6½ lengths in a Group 1 on its latest start, Dorset has solid credentials at this trip and should take to quick ground, though at 132 lb against likely improvers, a top-three finish may prove beyond a horse whose recent string suggests Group 3 level.

runners_data.name: Thesecretadversary
runners_data.note: Two wins from eight runs, both on good or similar ground, and has placed six times at 8f — stepping back to 7f here suits on paper; Heffernan partner holds a prominent position but needs to avoid being swamped in the early rush.
runners_data.comment: Held up without room at a crucial point in the Irish 2,000 Guineas last time, Thesecretadversary shaped better than a sixth-place finish suggests; a Group winner proven on today's going and a clear class edge dropping in grade makes this the one to beat from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Andab
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners this consistent O'Brien 3yo who has placed in five of his last seven starts; visor-equipped and ideally wants to race closer than the map allows given how many prominent types are crammed into this field.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without ever quite winning the argument at this level, Andab steps up in a visor for the first time from stall 12 carrying 129 lb, and while the mile trip and ground hold no fears, a 6-length third in Listed company last time out underlines both the solid form and the ceiling.

runners_data.name: Ardisia
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly arrives off a short 15-day turnaround with a moderate recent profile (three wins from 15 starts on similar going) and her natural forward style is crowded out; her best form has come over 6-7f but recent efforts have disappointed.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when a close-up third in Listed company on her latest start 15 days ago, and handles today's trip and conditions, though she may be best over a shorter six furlongs. Yet to win in her last five starts and carries 129 lb from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Avicenna
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's twice-winner is mapped to the rear having been redistributed from a prominent position as the most pace-uncommitted of those types; his 49-day break needs managing but he has won on good ground twice and carries a quiet dark-horse profile.
runners_data.comment: Showed smart form earlier in the season with back-to-back wins, though the Craven form has taken a few knocks and a well-beaten effort in the 2000 Guineas last time out raises questions; stepping back from Group 1 company helps, but 49 days off and 129 lb from stall 16 add to the puzzle.

runners_data.name: Billecart
runners_data.note: K R Burke hold-up specialist — one of the few genuinely natural backmarkers in the race — won at 8f on standard ground but 7f on good at Ascot is a sharp ask; Rowan Scott takes over and will need a strong pace to deliver from off it.
runners_data.comment: Sent to post 49 days ago and dropped back in from a Group 1 mauling at Newmarket, Billecart's ceiling now looks fairly clear despite that earlier win; acts on the going and trip, but ranked 14 of 17 on our figures, this good-looking colt has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Catullus
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby/William Buick combination always commands respect; won last time at Goodwood over 7f on good ground and has a solid 7f record (2W5P in 7 tries on similar going); redistributed to the rear in the map but his natural style is closer, which gives him a significant edge if he finds a prominent position.
runners_data.comment: Proven at today's trip and surface, and clearly thriving after wind surgery — that Goodwood win by four lengths on handicap debut was eyecatching, and there's a strong sense of more improvement to come. Dropping back after a 28-day break with 129 lb from stall 14, the step up in class is the key question.

runners_data.name: Colori Forever
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's 3yo has won twice over 7f on good ground and ran well on similar at Haydock; a front-running type by instinct but squeezed out of that role in this field, so his chance depends on how well he settles when held up against his will.
runners_data.comment: Hugely progressive with two wins in its last five starts — including a course success on this trip last time out — and clearly thriving, though a 43-day break and a tough 129 lb burden from stall 13 are factors to weigh against a step up in class.

runners_data.name: Into The Sky
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's progressive sort has won at 6f and placed at 8f on good ground; Oisin Murphy gives him a significant upgrade and he is one of the few here whose prominent position in the map is genuinely attainable given his natural forward-going style.
runners_data.comment: Scored on the same distance and going combination on offer here, but that Group 1 fourth last time — beaten 12 lengths when ridden up with the pace on what may not have been the best ground — raises questions about stamina, and a further drop in trip may suit best.

runners_data.name: Morris Dancer
runners_data.note: The Gosden yard's sole confirmed front-runner and pace anchor for this race; two wins on good ground over 7f, 311-day absence is a flag but he has the highest OR (110) and a trainer with an excellent strike rate from lay-offs; if he handles the return smoothly he shapes as structurally pivotal.
runners_data.comment: Carrying 129 lb from stall 8, Morris Dancer arrives on the back of a dominant Listed win at Salisbury with form since confirmed at Group level, suggesting there's more improvement to come at three — though 311 days off the track means this first run back may be needed.

runners_data.name: Neolithic
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's mount carries the blinkers flag and has won over 6f and 7f on good-to-soft; A P O'Brien operation in fine form (9/37 in 14 days) and Moore's positional intelligence may help him secure a prominent pitch ahead of rivals who are fighting for the same space.
runners_data.comment: Blinkers applied for the first time as Neolithic returns after 47 days, but this 107-rated runner sits 15th of 17 on our figures and must prove its soft-ground form translates on better going — a significant question mark. The top-grade jockey booking offers some hope.

runners_data.name: Saber Strike
runners_data.note: William Haggas/Tom Marquand send out an unexposed 3yo with a perfect 2-from-2 record, both wins on good ground at 6f and 7f — this trip is proven and the course could be; limited form to assess but the unbeaten profile and top connections make him a key prominent-pace beneficiary.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back victories — the latest a Listed success at Newmarket — mark Saber Strike as a horse potentially operating above this level, with trainer form an added boost; the 50-day absence and a stiff 129 lb are the questions to answer from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Take Charge Star
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's runner has a single win to show from five starts on similar going and is wearing a tongue-tie; a natural prominent runner who cannot secure that berth in this field and whose recent form (8th, 5th, 2nd, 6th, 1st) is mixed — discount the style-fit cost.
runners_data.comment: Stepped up to Group 1 company last time and beaten over eight lengths, Take Charge Star faces a similarly stiff task here as our 17th-ranked runner; the first-time headgear is worth noting, and from stall 1 over a familiar trip, there's some optimism — but this looks a tough ask.

runners_data.name: America Queen
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's filly has placed three times from four starts on good ground and won over 6f — stepping up to 7f at Ascot is the question; Loughnane keeps the ride and she is one of the genuine prominent types who should get close to her natural position in running.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck in a Group 3 on her latest start, America Queen has proven stamina for today's trip and handles this going, making her a genuine threat from stall 5 at 126 lb — though there's a question over whether she has more improvement to find.

runners_data.name: Domina Ignis
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's filly won over 6f on standard but her last two runs over 7f on good have been moderate (3rd, 18th); forced further back than her natural style allows given the field size, and her record suggests she has not yet proved she stays this trip under pressure.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up well below her best in the 1000 Guineas last time, Domina Ignis faces a stiff task from stall 11 off 126 lb, and our figures rank her 13th of 17. The Fred Darling third showed genuine grit, and the mile trip is within range, but that Group 1 flop is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Green Sense
runners_data.note: James McDonald is a powerful booking for Joseph Patrick O'Brien's 3yo, who won over 6f on soft last year but has been inconsistent since (including a 13th and 11th); displaced from a prominent position by superior pace competitors, his chance relies on McDonald manufacturing something from the middle of the pack.
runners_data.comment: Blocked for a run when fifth in a Group 2 last time out, Green Sense has excuses but still needs to find plenty given a ranking of 16th in the field; acts on today's conditions and should stay the trip, so not without hope if returning to form.

runners_data.name: The Prettiest Star
runners_data.note: Ed Walker/James Doyle pairing on a filly who has placed twice on good ground and won over 6f — she is one of the more lightly-raced runners here with an improving profile; a natural prominent runner who has a realistic chance of securing a good early pitch given her early pace and compact form.
runners_data.comment: Rockfel runner-up with Group 1 experience behind her, The Prettiest Star handles today's trip and conditions with authority and looks open to further progress — the 48-day absence is the one note of caution, though that Newmarket fourth suggests she returns in fine shape.

races.paceDynamic: Morris Dancer is the confirmed front-runner here and, with a field of 17 that is overwhelmingly populated by prominent-style horses, he is likely to find himself racing in a relatively uncontested lead position — a rare luxury in a Group 3 of this size. Into The Sky, America Queen, Thesecretadversary, Saber Strike and Neolithic are genuine prominent types who will press for position, but the sheer volume of pace-hungry runners means many — including Dorset, Andab, Ardisia, Colori Forever, Green Sense, Domina Ignis and Take Charge Star — cannot all secure their natural pitch and will be shuffled into a midfield mass, effectively racing out of role. The pace should be honest and sustained rather than frantically contested at the front, as Morris Dancer can dictate a rhythm with only a handful genuinely able to sit on his shoulder. This race shape most strongly favours horses who can race in the first three or four from an early position without fighting for it, and who carry a turn of foot into the final two furlongs on Good to Firm ground — true prominent runners who secure their position cleanly are structurally advantaged over the redistributed midfield pack.

watchPoints.text: Morris Dancer's 311-day absence is the single biggest race-shape risk — if he is ring-rusty and drops out quickly, the entire pace architecture collapses and the race becomes chaotic for all prominent types behind him.

With 17 prominent-style runners on a straight 7f, the first furlong will see a fierce scramble for position — watch for Dorset, Colori Forever and Take Charge Star being pushed wider or further back than connections intend, costing ground and energy.

Catullus (redistributed to hold-up in the map) is a natural prominent racer; if William Buick manages to push him forward to his true position, he becomes a much more dangerous proposition than his map placement suggests.

Saber Strike's unbeaten record masks an extremely thin form book — only two runs — meaning his sectional profile and response to a truly competitive Group 3 field is entirely unknown, creating significant pricing uncertainty around him.

Good to Firm conditions (confirmed in the going report despite the card listing Good) will sharpen the pace through the final two furlongs — horses who have previously shown a sharp finish on fast ground, notably Saber Strike and America Queen, gain a marginal but real edge.

races.name: Wokingham Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Spy Chief
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a clear lead in the absence of rivals for the position; William Buick will control fractions, and six course runs show consistent form on good, but his STYLE_FIT flag reflects that he races just off the pace by nature — leading is not his default mode, temper expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Placed when beaten a neck in a Listed race at Salisbury 28 days ago, Spy Chief is winless in his last five starts but that runner-up effort brings him close to his best; he handles today's trip and ground, though 7f could test his stamina, and he's run well at this track before.

runners_data.name: Soldier's Tree
runners_data.note: James Owen's five-year-old arrives on the back of a soft-ground win at Sandown but has limited good-ground evidence; De Sousa keeps it simple and Soldier's Tree will look to sit second or third, which suits the race shape, though the step back to handicap company from conditions events needs respect.
runners_data.comment: Consistent profile here, with that Salisbury Listed third last time arguably flattering the bare figures given traffic issues — yet still carrying 137 lb off a mark of 107 leaves little room for manoeuvre, even if there's improvement to come at this trip on suitable ground.

runners_data.name: Run Boy Run
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer runner with a visor, off 84 days but has a course win on good ground and won last time at Windsor on a going-to-good surface; has to be ridden from a prominent pitch and is proven at the trip, though the layoff and a crowded field add risk.
runners_data.comment: Scored narrowly in a Sprint Handicap at this mark three starts back before a poor latest effort, and first-time headgear plus a trainer in form add appeal — but 84 days off and a mark that may stretch him keep this a tentative each-way proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Double Rush
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old has won his last two starts on good ground at this exact distance and is one of the most in-form horses in the race on raw results; Shane Foley is well suited to big-field handicaps and Double Rush will sit prominently without overcomplicating matters — strong profile for the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins — the latest a comfortable success at Newmarket off a mark 10lb lower than today's — mark Double Rush as the one to beat here, and a top course handler takes the reins on a horse still looking ahead of its current official rating despite the penalty.

runners_data.name: Mitbaahy
runners_data.note: Charles Hills's seven-year-old hold-up horse carries a tongue-tie and comes back off 84 days, and his best form on good ground was two seasons ago; Billy Loughnane will be patient but finding clear passage through 28 runners from off the pace is a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Fitness must prove itself after 84 days away, with recent outings — including a poor effort in the Cammidge Trophy — leaving wellbeing in question; yet Mitbaahy is effective over this trip on any ground, and a bounceback to his placed form would make him a live midfield contender from stall 27.

runners_data.name: Binhareer
runners_data.note: William Haggas's four-year-old has won twice in six-furlong handicaps on good ground and Marquand has won big-field races before; pattern of form alternates placed and beaten runs which complicates the outlook, but the style fits well for a race where prominent runners with clean passages win.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck at York last time off a 5lb lower mark, Binhareer arrives here on the upgrade and looking capable of Listed/Group-level company, while a stiff track at today's trip plays to her strengths; 38 days between runs is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Two Tribes
runners_data.note: Off 106 days with a blinkers flag and two recent double-figure finishes suggesting he has gone off the boil; won here on good two starts ago but the form since then reads poorly, and the long layoff with a pattern of fading make him a watch-and-see rather than a confidence play.
runners_data.comment: Took a handicap by a short-head off this identical mark at Meydan in January, yet two unplaced efforts since suggest the handicapper has its measure, and 106 days off the track adds another question mark — albeit a form trainer and first-time headgear offer some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Heathcliff
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's five-year-old has most of his form at seven furlongs and on artificial or soft surfaces, with only one run at six on good in recent history; Cieren Fallon will look to place him prominently but the trip and going combination is a genuine query.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way on a turf return in a Listed heat last time, Heathcliff looks to have plenty to prove on grass and sits at the foot of our rankings — though a winning profile over the trip and decent AW form provide slim crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Dubai Bling
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's four-year-old is proven over six furlongs on good, has a pads flag, and Oisin Murphy provides top-level jockey quality in a key riding role; won here over six last time and the course-and-distance form is the most recent positive evidence in the race — a serious contender for the prominent scenario.
runners_data.comment: Touched off by a head last time out having encountered interference at a crucial point, Dubai Bling arrives in decent nick but carries 132lb from stall 23 in first-time cheekpieces, and a mark of 102 looks stiff for a horse our figures rank 25th of 28.

runners_data.name: Royal Zabeel
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's five-year-old has a mixed recent record, with the bulk of his better form on artificial surfaces; Jason Watson will try to track the pace but soft-ground and standard wins dominate, and the good-to-firm conditions may blunt him.
runners_data.comment: Listed winner in fair form and effective over today's trip on this going, Royal Zabeel brings solid credentials to stall 3 in a large field — though having found one too good for stamina close home when beaten two and a quarter lengths off this mark here last time, there are questions over whether it can go one better.

runners_data.name: Leovanni
runners_data.note: K R Burke's four-year-old returns off 119 days wearing a tongue-tie, with James McDonald a significant booking that commands attention; best form has come at five furlongs on good or standard, and stepping up to six with a layoff behind him makes this a bigger ask than the jockey name suggests.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts, Leovanni was making ground when hampered at Lingfield last time and shaped better than a two-length fourth suggests; a former Group winner now fitted with a tongue-tie returning from 119 days off, there's upside here if sharper for the break.

runners_data.name: Hammer The Hammer
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's four-year-old wears a tongue-tie and has been consistent without winning recently; form shows he sits close to the pace but fades in the closing stages, and with good-ground figures mostly negative, he is better watched than backed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but this second outing after a wind operation should see significant improvement — the York run was always about getting fit again. Capable of setting a strong pace over today's trip and going, though stall 7 may complicate that front-running style.

runners_data.name: Caburn
runners_data.note: James Tate's four-year-old is a natural prominent racer whose redistribution to midfield reflects the sheer volume of speed in this field; the pads flag and Colin Keane's ability to find position in big fields give him every chance of recovering his natural role, but a recent OR=100 form string ending in 30 does not inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Patchy recent form and a mark that looks tough to overcome are the main concerns, but first-time cheekpieces and a notable jockey booking add interest, and Caburn does handle this trip and going well enough to be competitive if producing a career-best.

runners_data.name: Roman Dragon
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's seven-year-old carries a visor and has a ⚠ fade flag that is damning in a race where he would need to close from off the pace; ran just 14 days ago and recent good-ground form is woeful — the fade warning combined with poor going figures makes him difficult to support.
runners_data.comment: Narrowly got up at Chester three starts back off a 5lb lower mark, but has been out of the frame twice since and the 100 rating looks a stiff ask — ranked near the foot of our assessments, first-time visor added from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Flash Harry
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's four-year-old, naturally prominent, is one of several similar types squeezed into the midfield on the map; the hood flag and a last-time-out sixth from a prominent position suggest he is not firing at his best, and the redistribution makes his chance contingent on an unusually open early scramble.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with a hood for the first time and carrying 130 lb from stall 26, Flash Harry has course-and-distance form to call on and has shown he can bounce back after a flat outing — his Salisbury run last time may have been needed on quicker ground than ideal, but fast conditions today suit, and a return to winning form isn't out of the question.

runners_data.name: Fandom
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old arrives on the back of a course-and-distance win 20 days ago and is one of the freshest positive form lines in the race; Sean Levey partnered him to that win and retains the ride, but being squeezed off his natural prominent pitch by the depth of pace in this field is the key risk — if he can recover position, his form says he belongs.
runners_data.comment: Thriving for a new yard after landing a Thirsk handicap last time, this US Listed winner arrives on a mark that still looks workable and has course-distance form to lean on, though that sixth in recent starts and a possible preference for faster ground give slight pause at 130 lb from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Far Above Dream
runners_data.note: James Owen's four-year-old has won four of his last five starts over six furlongs on good ground, including three consecutive victories; Kieran Shoemark has ridden him to all recent wins and knows the horse intimately — the redistribution to midfield on the map is structural, but his sheer winning momentum and proven course-and-distance ability make him one of the standout profiles in the race regardless of where he ends up.
runners_data.comment: Progressive and course-loving, but ranked 23 of 28 on our figures and lugging 129 lb from stall 17 off a career-high mark makes this a tough ask, despite four wins in the last five starts and a tendency to keep finding improvement.

runners_data.name: Ten Pounds
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer's patient and tactical style is a natural fit for a hold-up ride in a big field, but this five-year-old's recent form reading 48802 is deeply uninspiring; pads flag, and the going-to-good recent evidence of 2nd at Goodwood is a positive, but the overall form trajectory does not encourage.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with cheekpieces for the first time, Ten Pounds shaped with real promise when runner-up by just half a length in a Carlisle Listed contest last time out, and looks fairly handicapped off a mark of 99 with today's longer trip an additional plus — he can carry his head awkwardly under pressure.

runners_data.name: Completely Random
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride on Harry Charlton's five-year-old who has won twice on standard going and once on soft — good-to-firm is a real question mark; the redistribution reflects his genuine prominent style being crowded out, and Moore's ability to improvise is the main reason to keep him in scope.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces fitted for the first time could spark the turnaround after being left with it all to do from the rear at this course last time; yet to be beaten for today's jockey and progressive on this surface, though two unplaced efforts in recent starts demand respect.

runners_data.name: Thunderbear
runners_data.note: Jack Davison's six-year-old is a hold-up horse whose best form has come on good ground over six furlongs but with an overall trainer strike rate of 0/5 in the past 14 days; James Ryan is a capable northern rider but threading through 28 runners from the back is an enormous ask and the form string 514-60 does not suggest he is at peak fitness.
runners_data.comment: Thunderbear has yet to hit its stride this season and comes into this ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, with an unplaced effort last time out doing little to inspire confidence. A proven performer over the trip on varying ground at least offers some encouragement after 54 days off.

runners_data.name: Candy
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's four-year-old returns off 259 days — the longest absence in the field — with no prep run declared; last win came on soft going and the majority of form is on softer surfaces, making good-to-firm another concern on top of the fitness query.
runners_data.comment: Took the Ayr Silver Cup by two lengths off a 6lb lower mark two starts back, but flopped in Listed company most recently and returns after a 259-day absence; the trainer is in good nick and this trip and ground suit, though Candy may need the run to find full stride.

runners_data.name: Fast Track Harry
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's four-year-old, ridden by a 5lb claimer, has won twice on standard surfaces and struggles to confirm that form on good ground; the redistribution to midfield reflects a natural prominent style being squeezed back, and the combination of inexperienced rider, uncertain going preference, and big-field pressure makes this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 8¼ lengths at York last time after being sent to the front too soon, Fast Track Harry has since slipped to the bottom of the rankings despite two earlier wins in this sequence; he looks fully exposed to the assessor now, and first-time cheekpieces offer little obvious rescue from stall 21.

runners_data.name: Apollo One
runners_data.note: Christophe Soumillon is a high-class booking for this eight-year-old who won at this course on good ground two runs ago; ran 14 days ago, and the recent form reading 082939 is modest, but the pairing of elite jockey and course winner deserves inclusion as a potential each-way alternative.
runners_data.comment: Held every chance at Epsom 14 days ago but beaten five-plus lengths below form, leaving questions; yet to win in his last six starts, though the 2nd and 3rd suggest ability, his mark of 97 looks fair and he handles today's conditions.

runners_data.name: Evening Saigon
runners_data.note: Hamad Al Jehani's four-year-old has won twice on standard surfaces and posted a second on good, and the redistribution to midfield reflects his natural prominent style being compressed by the pace volume; positive recent form trend ending in a win and a second argues he is in form, though the leap to Royal Ascot handicap company is significant.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces go on for the first time, and there is some encouragement in a neck second last time off a mark of 92 — though today's conditions see this lightly raced sort stepping up 5lb, and ranked 20 of 28 on our figures, the case for it is thin.

runners_data.name: Realign
runners_data.note: William Haggas's four-year-old with a tongue-tie is ridden by James Doyle, who excels in big-field tactical races; won last time at Haydock on soft but has a good-ground Wolverhampton win in the profile — the going is not a definitive concern, but sitting in the redistributed midfield group when his natural style is prominent means clean air is the critical variable.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces did the trick at Carlisle 21 days ago when Realign won a handicap by 1¼l, but today's higher mark looks a stiff ask; acts on any turf ground over this trip and the trainer is firing at 37%, yet that 5lb rise in the official rating may take the edge off him.

runners_data.name: Toyotomi
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's five-year-old ran just 13 days ago, holds hold-up form credentials, and Daniel Tudhope has ridden him to his only win; best recent form came on soft ground and in races smaller than this, and from a genuine hold-up pitch in a 28-runner field the traffic challenge is formidable.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Goodwood handicap by a neck 13 days ago, dropping in class and getting a clear passage, and remains fairly treated on older French form — but ranked 22 of 28 on our figures, carrying 127 lb from stall 8 makes the task considerably stiffer here.

runners_data.name: Sondad
runners_data.comment: Sondad brings a recent win at Epsom on his side — taking a handicap by two lengths off a reduced mark — and a solid course record with proven versatility on the going, but ranked 21st of 28 on our figures, first-time headgear adds an unknown, and he faces a big field from stall 2 carrying 127 lb off a restored official mark of 97.

runners_data.name: Trefor
runners_data.comment: Showed a return to form when a staying-on fourth at Windsor 26 days ago, beaten three lengths off this same mark, but the official rating of 96 looks a stiff ask; effective at five-to-six furlongs on sound ground, though that late fade raises questions about lasting home.

races.paceDynamic: Spy Chief is the confirmed front-runner here and, critically, faces no serious rival for the lead — with one horse dictating from the front in a 28-runner field, the early pace will be honest but not frenetic, creating a controlled, rail-hugging gallop that stretches the field across the straight rather than bunching them. The sheer volume of prominent-style horses in this field — Double Rush, Binhareer, Dubai Bling, Soldier's Tree, Run Boy Run, Heathcliff and others — means the positions just off the leader will be fiercely contested, compressing the mid-section and making clean passage a serious concern for anything held up. That compressed, pressured chasing pack behind Spy Chief is the defining feature: those just behind the leader will burn energy scrimmaging for position, while the front two or three lengths of running space could prove a golden corridor. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently in the first three to five, who travel smoothly without having to fight for position — those are the horses most likely to have enough in reserve to sustain their effort over the final two furlongs on quick ground. Several redistributed runners including Far Above Dream, Flash Harry, Fandom, Caburn and Completely Random are genuine prominent types who will not all secure their natural position, and of those, Far Above Dream's exceptional course-and-distance record and Fandom's recent winning form give them the best credentials to fight through regardless.
