runners_data.name: Bourbon Blues
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who ran well in similar Good-ground conditions at 10f (second and third), and whose best form suits a race that develops late; 35 days off is fine for Brian Meehan's yard, and Joe Leavy takes the mount, but requires more pace than Sahara King alone is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and well held last time at Newbury, Bourbon Blues at least handles today's trip and conditions; the 135 lb burden is stiff, and a question mark lingers over whether that French Group form fully represents its true level.

runners_data.name: Sahara King
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and sole natural pace-setter; James Doyle will exploit an uncontested lead on fast ground, though the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is racing out of role relative to his wider form, and his three recent runs behind rivals suggest his solo-leader chance is better than his win strike-rate implies.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces go on for the first time as Sahara King steps up off a career-best effort — beaten a head at Newbury last time off a 6 lb lower mark — and with more likely to emerge over a trip and ground he handles well, he remains competitive from stall 17 on 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip on Good ground last time for Charlie Johnston and David Egan, which is the standout piece of form here; sits prominently by nature and has the tactical flexibility to slot just behind the early leader, making him one of the most naturally positioned horses in the race.
runners_data.comment: Steadily climbing the weights after a four-length Newmarket success, Evanesco handles today's conditions well over this trip, but 132 lb off a revised mark makes life considerably tougher than when scoring last time out 48 days ago.

runners_data.name: Spyce
runners_data.note: Prominently raced by Rossa Ryan and Alan King, but four runs over this course and distance without a win signals a possible ceiling; the form figures 214-54 show consistency without a breakthrough, and on a day with multiple prominent types competing for space he may find himself shuffled wider than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Beaten three and a half lengths off this very mark at Newbury last time out, Spyce shaped with promise on handicap debut yet may need a stiffer test to show his best; a tall, lightly raced colt who acts on today's conditions and rates unexposed at the trip.

runners_data.name: Bayaann
runners_data.note: Three runs, two wins, and already rated 98 for William Haggas — remarkably progressive; Cieren Fallon is a sharp judge of pace, only 12 days since last run is worth monitoring, but the horse won readily over 8f on Good and the step to 1m2f looks well within range for a horse with this trajectory.
runners_data.comment: Bayaann arrives in fine heart with two wins from three recent starts, including a determined display to beat a penalty burden at Windsor last time — debut form has been boosted since and he gets in on a fair opening mark of 98. The sole concern is whether this stiff 130 lb weight can be managed over the trip.

runners_data.name: Nil Bua Gan Dua
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's charge has contested this sort of ground repeatedly (five of five runs on Good), winning once and placing three times — a consistent sort; Dylan Browne McMonagle rides, and a horse that sits prominently and handles the conditions reliably is always a factor in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winning at Roscommon 40 days ago over an extended trip suggests this two-year-old has more to offer in handicaps, and the form looks solid — but ranked bottom of the field on our figures with a speed rating of 62, it faces a stiff ask from stall 11 off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Harmonics
runners_data.note: Won his last two starts including a 10f Goodwood success on Good ground, giving him the best recent form of any prominent-style runner; the John & Thady Gosden yard are firing (7 from 36 in 14 days) and Shane Foley has ridden him before — 15 days between runs is straightforward for this operation.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in its last three starts, including a six-length novice success at Doncaster, Harmonics arrives in good nick but ranks 12th of 16 on our figures, and the penalty of 129lb in a competitive handicap makes this a considerably tougher ask.

runners_data.name: Sunset On Leros
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse, flagged as such with the headgear note, and Marco Ghiani is an assured judge from the rear; the 50-day absence is the only concern, but the horse won over 7f on Good and placed twice over further on the same surface, and if the race develops any late pace he will be finishing.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces applied for the first time as Sunset On Leros steps up in trip, which breeding suggests should suit, and she showed renewed spark on turf at San Siro last time; however, 50 days between runs and a mark of 97 make this a tough ask against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Balzac
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's gelding is a natural prominent runner whose most recent runs include solid thirds over 10f and 12f on Good ground, but with the field crowded at the front he is pushed back to midfield on the map — Billy Loughnane must navigate carefully from a compromised position, and the STYLE_FIT discount is warranted.
runners_data.comment: Balzac has placed three times in recent starts and handles today's trip and conditions, but his last two outings have exposed limitations at the top level, and the official mark of 97 leaves him plenty to find on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Amadeus Mozart
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes a ride on a horse who has won over 7f and placed at 10f and 12f, showing versatility; a natural front-running type who will be forced to settle further back than he wants given the competition for prominent berths, and Moore's ability to find a position mid-race is the key to whether he can overcome that disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in his last four starts and running to peak level when runner-up at Listed level latest, Amadeus Mozart brings strong recent form over today's trip with a top jockey aboard, though the shortened distance may blunt his edge.

runners_data.name: Lost Boys
runners_data.note: James McDonald partners a horse with three wins from his last five starts and the best win-rate of any runner in the race; a natural prominent runner displaced to midfield by the crowded field, his Good-ground 10f wins are directly relevant, but McDonald will need early luck in running to avoid being hemmed in.
runners_data.comment: Winning three of its last five starts looks eye-catching, but Lost Boys faces a considerably tougher assignment off a career-high mark now, and our figures rank it 14th of 16 — a stiff ask, even for a horse that clearly stays the trip and acts on a sound surface.

runners_data.name: Allegresse
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy on a hold-up filly who won her first two starts but has since finished fourth and ninth — the form has softened; she is a genuine closer and Murphy will have her back in the field, meaning she needs pace ahead of her that this race shape may not consistently provide.
runners_data.comment: Connections landed this race last year and Allegresse handles today's trip and surface well, but stamina remains unproven and those back-to-back wins now feel a while ago — the latest ninth at Epsom, where softer ground likely told, clouds the picture from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Perisher
runners_data.note: William Buick on a horse who has won his last two (most recently over 10f on Good) and is trained by Joseph O'Brien — a strong combination; a natural prominent type who must race further back than ideal given the traffic, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers enthusiasm despite the solid recent form.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins and an impressive 4½-length success at Naas last time out make Perisher the one to beat here; a significant jockey booking adds further confidence, and though the first-time hood is worth monitoring, this consistent performer looks well treated returning to a handicap over a familiar trip.

runners_data.name: Princling
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand and William Haggas have placed this horse four times in four career starts, including a win over 8f and a 10f place on Good ground; a natural front-runner squeezed from his position, he has the ability but the competition for space at the head of affairs makes this assignment difficult.
runners_data.comment: His pedigree points to this longer trip suiting, Princling showed plenty on his recent handicap debut at Carlisle when going down by just 2½ lengths off a lower mark, and he moves like one the step up to 10f will improve. The fourth last time out is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Folk Pageant
runners_data.note: Rowan Scott partners a horse who has won four of his last five starts, all over 10f on Good or Soft — a relentless progressive improver; naturally prominent and has clearly found his level at this trip, but the redistribution to midfield means Scott must work to recover ground that this horse does not naturally cede.
runners_data.comment: Folk Pageant arrives on the back of a strong recent run — three wins from its last five starts — but a hefty rise in the weights and a step up in grade make this a considerably sterner test, and at 15th of 16 on our figures it's hard to make a strong case.

runners_data.name: Echo Of Stars
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer, one of the most patient jockeys in the weighing room, takes the ride on a horse wearing a tongue-tie who won last time over 10f on Good ground; a natural prominent type remapped to midfield, Spencer's tactical acumen is the biggest asset here if the race develops into a cavalry charge from the turn.
runners_data.comment: Broke through at Chepstow last time in a tongue-tie, scoring by 2¼ lengths, and stays on a mark of 90 with potentially more to offer now in handicap company — but ranked 13 of 16 on our figures makes this a difficult proposition to get excited about.

races.paceDynamic: Sahara King is the confirmed front-runner and, as the sole genuine pace-setter in a 17-runner field, will attempt to control from the gate at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Ascot. With no natural rival to push the tempo, the pace is unlikely to be searching, creating a race that could be run at a measured clip before accelerating in the straight — conditions that typically reward horses sitting close to the action rather than those making up ground from the rear. The field, however, holds far more prominent types than can all occupy their natural positions: Balzac, Lost Boys, Amadeus Mozart, Perisher, Princling, Folk Pageant and Echo Of Stars are all genuine front-to-prominent horses redistributed to midfield on the map, and in reality Harmonics, Nil Bua Gan Dua, Bayaann, Evanesco and Spyce are the most likely to actually secure prominent berths behind Sahara King given their established styles and connections. The tactical verdict is clear: a single, uncontested leader setting a controlled pace on fast ground over this trip at Ascot heavily favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace — those able to track the moderate tempo and have something left when the race quickens from the turn in.

With seven or more natural prominent types competing for four or five positions behind Sahara King, watch for crowding and bumping on the turn into the back straight — Balzac, Lost Boys and Amadeus Mozart are most likely to be squeezed and forced widest.

Sahara King must be tracked throughout — if James Doyle is allowed to build a three-length lead unchallenged through the first six furlongs on fast ground, the leader becomes a live danger that the map underestimates.

races.name: Queen Alexandra Stakes (Conditions Race) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: A Piece Of Heaven
runners_data.note: Consistent at this sort of trip and beyond, with strong placed form in similar conditions (good); Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for O'Brien and this horse races prominently — 43 days off but horses the stable has returned after gaps have run well; goes on good ground and handles 15f+, stepping up to 2m5½f is the key unknown but the long-distance form gives confidence.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and progressive, A Piece Of Heaven arrives on the back of a Chester handicap win — forging clear from the front over a testing trip — and clearly handles today's going and distance range; first-time headgear under 130 lb is the one factor to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Sundance
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner by nature — Balding's six-year-old wants to be up with the pace — but with so many prominent types in this field, Murphy is likely to find himself shuffled into a midfield role against the horse's instincts; best form has come when making the running on Lingfield's Polytrack and that stamina-laden profile may count if the trip suits, but the positional compromise is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: Showed good form prior to that Chester run 43 days ago where stamina appeared to stretch, and first-time headgear plus a trainer who excels here offer encouragement — but 130 lb and that question over the trip make this a genuine each-way proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Carlton
runners_data.note: James Owen's six-year-old has winning form over 20f at Goodwood and placed at 14f+ on good ground, showing this trip is within scope; a natural forwardly-placed horse who will struggle to assert that instinct today given the volume of early movers — Cieren Fallon will likely have to settle for a position further back than ideal, softening the chance in a slowly-run race.
runners_data.comment: Carlton has been placed in its last two outings and clearly handles today's going, but ranked 10 of 13 on our figures and needing to find more stepping up in class, this 130lb burden makes it tough to get excited, despite genuine stamina in its favour.

runners_data.name: Columbus
runners_data.note: Mullins' five-year-old has placed at 20f on good ground (2nd at Royal Ascot in the Hardwicke route), so the trip is not an issue; Colin Keane takes the ride and this horse wants to be in the first half of the field — 244 days off with only a 40-day jumps run intervening is the significant flag, and that absence from flat competition at this level must be respected despite the obvious class.
runners_data.comment: Columbus arrives here winless in his last five starts but shaped with plenty of encouragement on his hurdles debut at Killarney, finishing second before weakening close home — fitness should sharpen with that run under his belt. A classy Flat performer in France effective over 12-15f, he's no second-string runner here, and connections landed this prize last year.

runners_data.name: Dallas Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for De Aguiar who has been busy of late (22 days since last run) and posted placed efforts at 14-16f on good ground, though has yet to win over any of these trips; needs a stronger pace than Illinois is likely to provide, and on good-to-firm the closing ground will be firm enough to stretch his stamina reliance — the modest OR of 101 also makes this hard to win from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and rated 11th of 13 on our figures, Dallas Star faces a stiff task carrying 130 lb, and the latest fourth at Down Royal — racing prominently over 2m — hinted the extra distance stretches stamina. Back at 14f could help.

runners_data.name: French Master
runners_data.note: Gosden's five-year-old boasts a strong record on good ground — 8 runs on similar footing, 3 wins — and won over 14f before being stepped up; James Doyle steers a prominent-racing type whose natural inclination suits the likely race shape well; the 35-day gap is straightforward and the hat (headgear p) suggests he needs covered ground, which this trip provides — the concern is whether 2m5½f stretches him beyond his optimum.
runners_data.comment: Fresh headgear goes on for the first time in cheekpieces, and while French Master's most recent effort — a well-held fifth in a Group 3 — was a letdown, this horse has been largely consistent otherwise, handles today's going well, and a trainer firing at 26% adds confidence. The worry is that last outing in headgear underwhelmed.

runners_data.name: Hipop De Loire
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield trains the nine-year-old who shows blinkered (b) and has won over marathon trips before, but recent form (4630-7) is moderate and the last run was 7th; George Wood rides a horse that by nature wants to race prominently but the sheer weight of pace in this field means he is likely to find himself in a midfield position far removed from his comfort zone — at OR 102 with this current form it is hard to make a strong case.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and well beaten at Goodwood on a latest flat outing, Hipop De Loire arrives here in first-time blinkers off a 28-day break, though a course-and-distance-proven handler in form and a useful German Listed background offer some grounds for hope.

runners_data.name: Illinois
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's mount is the confirmed pace-maker of this field and will set the gallop from flagfall — the question is whether Moore applies enough tempo at 2m5½f to prevent a dawdle, and at OR 111 (highest in the field) the class is evident; the [STYLE_FIT] flag is a quirk of the field composition rather than a concern about Illinois's role, as he genuinely wants to lead; 14 days since last run is ideal freshness and the Aidan O'Brien stable runs at 37% over the past 14 days.
runners_data.comment: His second in the Gold Cup over course and distance is the strongest form on offer here, and though Illinois was asked only to set the gallop at Epsom last time out, this smart stayer returns to a track and trip that suit on going it handles, partnered by the course's standout jockey.

runners_data.name: Le Destrier
runners_data.note: William Buick partners the Mullins seven-year-old who has placed at 12-14f on good and heavier ground — the step to 2m5½f is a substantial extension from his established form range and is the primary concern; a genuine hold-up horse with limited flat runs (four in the history shown), so the pace scenario must play into his hands, and the lack of exposed stamina at this extreme trip cannot be overlooked even for an O'Brien-Mullins combination.
runners_data.comment: Freshened after a creditable third in the Levmoss Stakes (Group 3) at Leopardstown — where he was checked and still closed — Le Destrier travels well for a stable that landed this last year and should be suited by this trip and ground; the slight concern is that his recent consistency has been mixed.

runners_data.name: Maxi King
runners_data.note: De Foy's six-year-old has a second at 18f on good ground (Ascot form) which is directly relevant to this contest, and Rowan Scott has experience with the horse; prominently-placed by style and likely to get closer to his natural position than some of the more extreme prominent types; the OR of 103 is mid-field and he doesn't carry the headgear or significant concerns — a quiet each-way profile if the race is run to suit prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Consistent but winless in his last five starts, Maxi King at least caught the eye when a narrow second over an extended trip at Chester 43 days ago, showing his stamina holds over distance — though connections will need that improvement to translate here off 130lb.

runners_data.name: Mr Hollywood
runners_data.note: Mullins' six-year-old has hold-up form over 20f on good ground (3rd) and the trip suits on paper, but 269 days off (with only a 40-day jumps run intervening) is a major fitness concern at this level; Billy Loughnane takes the ride and at OR 98 the ceiling is modest — genuine hold-up type who needs a strong pace and clean air, conditions that may not materialise with Illinois setting a controlled tempo.
runners_data.comment: Switched to a top yard that won this race last year and with more improvement likely, Mr Hollywood's winning form and solid placed efforts are in his favour, though weakening late on his most recent hurdle start hints he may not yet be fully wound up.

runners_data.name: Aajej
runners_data.note: Richard Phillips' four-year-old is the most lightly-weighted runner (129lbs) and youngest in the field, showing a win over 14f on Tapeta but limited turf form on good ground — the sim-going record on turf reads 0 wins from 3 attempts; a hold-up horse by inclination who wants a pace to close into, and at OR 77 faces a significant class hike; Kieran Shoemark has the experience but this feels like a race too far for the profile.
runners_data.comment: Ninth of nine last time out, beaten nine lengths in a handicap here, raises real stamina doubts over this trip, and first-time cheekpieces won't mask those concerns. A 77-rated sort carrying 129lb, ranked near the foot of our figures.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Days
runners_data.note: Syd Hosie's four-year-old is the outsider of the party at OR 63 — a true hold-up horse pushed into the midfield mapping by the volume of closers in this field — and 105 days off (29-day jumps run only) raises serious fitness questions; best form has come over shorter trips on good ground and the step to 2m5½f represents an enormous stamina test for an unexposed stayer; George Downing takes the ride but this is a very big ask on every metric.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and poor in both codes this term, Pivotal Days faces a stiff ask here — ranked last on our figures and seemingly out of its depth in this company, though the going should suit.

races.paceDynamic: Illinois is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with Ryan Moore in the saddle, will dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this extended 2m5½f trip on good-to-firm ground — a setup that rewards those who can travel economically and produce a finish rather than those who need an honest, end-to-end test. The field contains a significant surplus of prominent types: Berkshire Sundance, Hipop De Loire, Carlton, A Piece Of Heaven, French Master, Columbus, and Maxi King all want to race up with or near the pace, meaning several will be unable to secure their natural position and will effectively be running in midfield against their instincts. Of those prominent types, Illinois, A Piece Of Heaven, French Master, and Columbus are most likely to actually secure early positions, with the others shuffled back into a compressed midfield. The resulting shape — a steady single pace-setter, a bunched mid-division, and a clean run into the straight — strongly favours horses who can race handily in the first half of proceedings and produce a sustained gallop home, rather than true hold-up types who need a stronger pace to close into.

watchPoints.text: Illinois and Ryan Moore control everything — if Moore elects to go even more slowly than expected through the first mile, the race risks becoming a dash from two furlongs out that disadvantages all genuine hold-up types (Dallas Star, Le Destrier, Mr Hollywood) and inflates the chance of the prominent-tracking horses behind him.

The surplus of prominent types (Berkshire Sundance, Hipop De Loire, Carlton) who cannot get their natural positions will create a compressed and potentially scrappy mid-division — watch for early positional jostling in the first half-mile as these horses try to assert against their suppressed instincts, which could cause interference further back.

Columbus and Mr Hollywood both return from long absences (244 and 269 days respectively) having only had jumps runs as prep — monitor market support and any late market moves for either, as Mullins has the capacity to produce horses fit from such breaks but the risk is real for both.

French Master's going record (8 runs, 3 wins on good) is the standout surface statistic in the field — if conditions ride on the faster end of good-to-firm (which the going report for this race suggests), his profile strengthens materially and he could be the one best suited to make a sustained challenge to Illinois.

Le Destrier has only four flat runs in the history shown and has never been tested beyond 14f on the flat — William Buick will need to produce a masterclass in pace judgement over this marathon trip, and any sign of the horse travelling awkwardly or struggling to hold his position early would be an immediate negative signal.
